issue_context.title: Adjust watch bookmark policy to match watch-cache size policy
issue_context.body:
Currently, (best-effort) watch bookmarks are sent just right before the given watch is supposed to timeout:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3b00d7dce51b3833815e2459e3a92ed917402170/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L1243

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90091 we're adjusting how the size of watch cache is determined and make it dynamic and more duration-oriented (rather than based on some magic constants) - we're targeting to always keep 5 minutes of history in watch cache.

With that change, we should get back to our bookmark policy:
- change it to (additionally to right before timeout) also send bookmarks every N seconds (setting N to slightly less than expected watch cache history period, so slightly less than X minutes we will use there)
- scale-test this change (to see if it doesn't introduce non-negligible overhead)
- if so permanently introduce this change

/sig scalability api-machinery
comments: I'm reverting #90249 as it broke bookmarks. I'm going to fix and re-submit for review hopefully later this week.

review_comments: QQ: Is it possible (watch without deadline/timeout) or is it just a safe check?

If you're using our framework like reflector - it will always be set:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L387
We also try to default it it is't not provided:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go#L249

But you may configure it in a way to not provide minRequestTimeout, and then it may happen (though in properly configuder custer it shouldn't happen).
